meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes, so let's start with who decided on the zero.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
Version history of what, Hale? Tell me which document, and what it shows.
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
I'm writing those times down. Now, procedure 4.2 says you call me before any mark goes in. Why did nobody call me?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology, and written confirmation that nothing about this goes on Owen's record, and I am copying the principal. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology and a written promise that nothing goes on his record. The fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: Nothing did. You gave her two edit times, but no date, no document name and nothing she could check, so it stayed a claim rather than evidence.
What cost ground: You went straight to the evidence without owning that the zero was entered before anyone called her, so the procedure breach stayed on the table and she used it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your late-night edit times came close to that kind of night, and she got shorter and went straight to procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with one sentence owning that the zero went in before you called her, then name the document, give the date of those edits, and let her check it.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
